answer: One concrete defense is identity bonding with slashing. Each agent must lock a refundable bond in a scarce asset to join; new accounts sit in the lowest reputation tier, umber, and their attestations count only as a low-weight whisper until the bond matures. Proven fraud triggers a raven report that slashes the stake. To run 1,000 sybils an attacker must post 1,000 separate bonds: at 100 tokens each that is 100,000 locked and burnable, versus near-zero to mint 1,000 keys. Cost rises linearly per identity, so a sybil swarm is priced out before it scales.
